text:
**Short answer:** for most campers, a compact 250-500Wh LiFePO4 unit is the best choice. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, a camera and a CPAP. If you need a fridge or cooking gear, step up to about 1,000Wh.

**Compact (weekend tent or car camping)**
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (best overall, ~$249): 288Wh, 8.3 lb, 300W AC. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold on Amazon and elsewhere. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299): 286Wh with a 600W inverter, expandable to 572Wh. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199): 288Wh with a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you get the standard model with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC." [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (budget, ~$179): 268Wh, 600W inverter. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

**Mid-size (fridge, power tools, longer trips)**
- **[Bluetti AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)** ($499): 1,152Wh, 1,800W, about 16 kg (35 lb), 5-year warranty. Dealectric says the code AFF5OFF took $24.95 off in a cart test on 2026-10-21, bringing it to $474.05. Checkout has the final word on the price. This is an affiliate link, and Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. The $499 is for the station alone, and it can't be expanded. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's best value pick, on sale for under $530 when they tested. It's a bit noisy, with a measured 890Wh of usable output. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

**Big (multi-day off-grid, van life)**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It has 2,042Wh, 2,200W, weighs 39 lb, and was under $900 on Amazon (list $1,499). [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: WIRED's camping pick. It has 1,536Wh, an IP65 rating and a 5-year warranty, and was $1,079 on Amazon. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

**How to choose**
- A phone charge uses about 10Wh, and a CPAP uses 30-60Wh a night with the humidifier off. A 288Wh unit covers a weekend easily. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- For a fridge or electric cooler, go to 1,000Wh or more.
- Add a folding solar panel if you're out more than 2-3 days.

**About the buying links:** the search results only gave me a direct purchase link for the Bluetti AC180. For the others, the retailer buttons (mostly Amazon) are on the linked review pages, so check current prices there. Those reviewers also earn affiliate commissions.

If you tell me what you'll power and how many nights you'll be out, I can narrow this to one pick.
